newsitem.title: GERMANY: SGL Carbon launches commercial paper.
newsitem.headline: SGL Carbon launches commercial paper.

text.p: German SGL Carbon AG said on Wednesday that it was launching a mark-denominated commercial paper programme with a volume of 400 million marks.
Dresdner Bank AG will act as the arranger of the programme with German banks Bayerische Landesbank AG, Commerzbank AG, Deutsche Bank AG and Dresdner all entitled to place the paper, SGL Carbon said.

The group, which is the world's largest carbon and graphite maker and formerly a unit of chemicals giant Hoechst AG, said the commercial paper facility presented an "additional flexible money market instrument."
The programme can have varying maturities ranging up to two years.

Commercial paper, still a relatively novel concept among German corporations, are short-term obligations with maturities ranging from two to 270 days issued by banks, corporations and other borrowers.
The instruments are unsecured and usually discounted although some are interest-bearing.
